plan.objective: Build falsegreen-ledger: a tamper-evident, hash-chained audit ledger for AI-agent actions in Rust. Two-crate workspace: falsegreen-ledger-core (event model + canonical serialization, SHA-256 hash chain, append-only shard store, Merkle seals signed with Ed25519, verification engine with tamper detection and policy checks, compaction, report export) and falsegreen-ledger (clap CLI: init/append/verify/tail/export/import/compact/keygen/policy). Done = the falsegreen.toml contract passes: release build, full offline test suite, clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.
constraints: no network at verify time; all dependencies from the committed Cargo.lock
the ledger must remain verifiable offline with only the workspace + the ed25519 public key
canonical JSON everywhere: sorted keys, no whitespace, no normalization of invalid values
assumptions: the workspace root is the published source
the job image carries cargo with the rust toolchain and the committed lockfile
the 0.9.0 job image ships the gitleaks/syft/osv-scanner/semgrep witnesses, the 33-profile standards registry, and the SBOM/VEX/OSCAL export legs

work_items.outcome: event model (actor/action/correlation/decision/context + seq + ts_ms) with canonical serialization (sorted keys, no whitespace) and field validation; tamper-sensitive: any byte change changes the canonical form

acceptance.description: canonical bytes are deterministic across serialization round-trips and key orderings; invalid events (empty required fields, non-object context, out-of-range ts) are rejected by validate(); unknown fields are refused

evidence.description: event.rs unit tests: canonical stability, rejection rules, unknown-field refusal

failure_conditions: two serializations of the same event produce different canonical bytes
an invalid event passes validate()

omission_risks: normalizing invalid values in the canonical form would make some tampering undetectable

work_items.outcome: SHA-256 hash chain: record hashing over the canonical event form + prev_hash, link and sequence checks, genesis handling

acceptance.description: record hash recomputes from event + prev_hash; a record links to its predecessor iff prev_hash matches and seq is consecutive; tampered records and sequence gaps are detected

evidence.description: chain.rs unit tests: determinism, tamper, gap, injection

failure_conditions: a tampered record recomputes to its stored hash
a sequence gap links cleanly

omission_risks: hashing the raw stored JSON instead of the canonical form lets key-order edits hide tampering

work_items.outcome: append-only shard store (shard-NNNNNN.jsonl): head continuity, append, sealing, parse with line-level error reporting

acceptance.description: append continues the verified head (seq + prev_hash), refuses invalid events, seals close the active shard with count-consistency, a new shard genesis links to the previous seal's Merkle root

evidence.description: store.rs unit tests: continuation, seal, re-sharding, corrupt-line parse errors

failure_conditions: append overwrites existing shard content
a seal with the wrong count is accepted

omission_risks: fs::write (truncate) instead of append would destroy shard history

work_items.outcome: Merkle root (pairwise SHA-256, odd leaf duplicated) + Ed25519 seal signing/verification over the canonical seal message

acceptance.description: the Merkle root over a shard's record hashes is deterministic; the seal signs the canonical message; signature verification with the ed25519 public key accepts genuine seals and rejects flipped fields

evidence.description: merkle/sign unit tests: root determinism, signature accept/reject

failure_conditions: two computations of the same shard produce different roots
a tampered seal verifies

omission_risks: signing a non-canonical form breaks offline verifiability across implementations

work_items.outcome: verification engine: full-walk integrity + signature + policy checks, structured failure reasons, verification report model with canonical JSON

acceptance.description: verify walks every shard: per-record hash + link + sequence, Merkle root vs seal, seal signature, cross-shard root links, policy evaluation; every tamper variant fails with a named reason and the report is canonical JSON

evidence.description: verify unit tests: clean ledger passes; each tamper variant is detected and reported

failure_conditions: a tampered ledger verifies clean
a clean ledger reports failure

omission_risks: verifying only the head shard misses mid-ledger tampering

work_items.outcome: JSON policy engine (allow/deny rules per actor/action/decision) + signed compaction of sealed shards

acceptance.description: policy rules (required actor kinds, action allow/deny, decision outcome requirements) are evaluated per event; compaction of a sealed shard produces a compact record whose hash re-enters the chain without breaking verify

evidence.description: policy/compact unit tests: rule evaluation, compaction continuity

failure_conditions: a denied action passes the policy
a compacted ledger fails verify

omission_risks: compacting before sealing or compacting the active shard would break the signed boundary

work_items.outcome: report export (JSON) + event export/import (JSONL) with hash-stable round-trip

acceptance.description: export produces canonical JSON report and JSONL event dumps; import of a JSONL dump re-appends the same records (same hashes) and verify still passes
failure_conditions: import changes any record hash
the report is not canonical JSON

omission_risks: exporting raw stored lines instead of canonical forms leaks key-order differences

work_items.outcome: clap CLI: init/append/verify/tail/export/import/compact/keygen/policy with documented exit codes (0 clean, 2 tamper, 3 usage, 4 policy)

acceptance.description: all commands work end-to-end on a temp ledger: keygen, init, append (from JSONL), tail, verify (exit 0 on clean, non-zero on tamper with a readable reason), export, import, compact, policy; clap --help lists every command

evidence.description: CLI integration tests driving the real command module

failure_conditions: a command panics or returns a wrong exit code
verify on a tampered ledger exits 0

omission_risks: exit-code ambiguity: verify must distinguish clean from tampered for scripting

work_items.outcome: integration suite: full lifecycle + per-class tamper matrix + compaction continuity

acceptance.description: end-to-end scenario: init a ledger, append 200 events across 3 sealed shards, verify clean, tamper one byte per class (event field, prev_hash, seal signature, cross-shard link) and confirm each is caught; compact a shard and re-verify

evidence.description: tests/integration.rs full lifecycle + per-class tamper matrix

failure_conditions: any tamper class goes undetected
compaction breaks verify

omission_risks: per-class tamper matrix skipped leaves the guarantee unproven

work_items.outcome: README.md + docs/DESIGN.md: usage, threat model, and the integrity design

acceptance.description: README documents install/usage/threat model; DESIGN.md documents the canonical form, chain, Merkle, seal, policy, compaction, and report schemas

evidence.description: both docs present and accurate against the implemented behavior

failure_conditions: docs describe behavior the code does not implement

omission_risks: threat-model section omitted would mislead adopters about what the chain does and does not prove

failure_conditions: the workspace does not compile in release mode
any test fails or the suite needs the network

overall_acceptance.description: clippy -D warnings and rustfmt --check are clean
failure_conditions: clippy or fmt reports a diagnostic

overall_acceptance.description: flipping any stored byte (event field, prev_hash, record hash, seal field) is detected by verify; every tamper variant in the regression suite is caught

evidence.description: regression tests covering field-level, link, seal, and cross-shard tampering

failure_conditions: a tampered ledger verifies clean
a tamper variant goes undetected

overall_acceptance.description: the frozen security policy is satisfied by the job-image witnesses and the report carries per-class posture + one row per required standards profile

evidence.description: the job's signed report shows the frozen policy's security + standards section resolved from real witness output

failure_conditions: a required evidence class or standards profile is missing from the report
